samples_reviewed.question_text: In 1695, what digit is in the ones place?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: I hand-checked all 8 items against the 4-digit place structure: digit 5 in 5210 is thousands (place value 5000, seed 45), digit 1 in 1420 is thousands (1000, seed 47), digit 1 in 3615 is tens (seed 48), digit 4 in 4120 is thousands (seed 49); every stated answer is arithmetically correct.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The 8 seeds test ones (42, 44, 46), tens (43, 48), and thousands (45, 47, 49) positions, but no sample asks about the hundreds digit specifically even though every 4-digit number shown has one, leaving that position untested in this particular batch.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The question frame is identical in structure to the grade-1 and grade-2 sibling nodes, appropriately scaled only by number size (4 digits) for grade-3 quarter-1 readers rather than by added sentence complexity.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: This batch now includes genuine reverse-lookup items ('In 1695, what digit is in the ones place?', seed 42; 'In 3615, what digit is in the tens place?', seed 48), correcting the gap the prior stale review flagged as entirely missing for this lc.

competency_alignment.rationale: The metadata lists 'ten-thousands place' as vocabulary introduced by this node, but the competency text and every one of the 8 samples cap out at 4-digit numbers whose highest position is thousands (e.g. 5210, 4120), so the stated new vocabulary does not actually match what the generated content teaches.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: 4-digit numbers (1420 to 9105) with place values up to 5000 correctly match the grade-3 quarter-1 scope of thousands-place introduction, staying within a single new order of magnitude beyond the grade-2 3-digit sibling.
